description: Return a directional RUB production range and timeline only when the user explicitly asks about price, cost, budget, quote, or budget fit. This tool is read-only, non-binding, and never collects contact details or submits a brief. Choose WHOLE_PRODUCTION for a finished deliverable and BOUNDED_SHOT_POST for named shots/scenes/post work; use INFERRED when that scope is genuinely ambiguous, or SCENARIO for a clearly labeled hypothetical. For production diagnosis without pricing, use diagnose_production instead.

assumptions.description: Explicit factual assumptions used to make the estimate possible; do not invent client facts.

deadlineDays.description: Calendar days available until delivery when known; null or omit when no deadline is supplied.

exclusions.description: Work explicitly outside this estimate, especially live-action, rights, media, extra versions, or unrequested disciplines.

externalBidItems.description: Known cost exposures that require third-party bids; these remain outside the automated production range.

label.description: External cost item that cannot be responsibly priced by this engine, such as talent, location, licensed music, or live-action vendor work.

reason.description: Why this cost requires an external quote or remains unknown.

includeDepartments.description: Optional whitelist of departments to include when the requested estimate intentionally covers only selected disciplines.

mode.description: ROM for an early range; SCOPED_ESTIMATE for a defined scope; BUDGET_FIT to compare scope with a target budget; DEADLINE_FIT to evaluate schedule pressure.

runtimeSeconds.description: Final master runtime in seconds when known; null only when genuinely unknown.

scopeBasis.description: One concise sentence stating exactly what the estimate includes and excludes from the priced object.

scopeDecision.description: USER_EXPLICIT when the requested object is clear; SCENARIO for an explicitly labeled hypothetical; INFERRED only when scope is genuinely ambiguous, in which case no price is returned until clarified.

scopeEvidence.description: Short evidence for the scope choice. For USER_EXPLICIT, copy a brief verbatim phrase from the user's request that identifies the priced object.

scopeType.description: WHOLE_PRODUCTION prices the complete requested finished deliverable; BOUNDED_SHOT_POST prices only named shots, scenes, VFX, or post tasks.

targetBudgetMax.description: Upper bound of the user's target budget in RUB for BUDGET_FIT; omit when no target ceiling is supplied.

targetBudgetMin.description: Lower bound of the user's target budget in RUB for BUDGET_FIT; omit when no budget floor exists.

units.description: Production line items that drive the estimate. Include every material discipline/unit being priced; each item explains quantity, complexity, locks, continuity, and basis.

basis.description: Short factual notes explaining why this unit, quantity, complexity, or lock count was chosen.

complexity.description: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or EXTREME execution complexity for this unit.

department.description: Department responsible for this unit; use the closest production discipline from the enum.

hardLocks.description: Number of exact visual constraints this unit must preserve, such as product geometry, identity, logo, camera, or wardrobe.

id.description: Stable short ID for this production unit, such as hero-shots, compositing, or edit.

quantity.description: Count of comparable units in this line item. Defaults to 1 when omitted.

recurringEntities.description: Count of products, characters, vehicles, or other entities that must stay consistent across multiple outputs.

reusable.description: True when the unit creates a reusable asset/system that materially reduces repeated production work.

versioning.description: Version/adaptation workload beyond the master deliverable; distinguish simple exports from recomposition and new production.

derivedVersions.description: Count of low-effort versions derived from the master without new composition or production.

newProductionUnits.description: Count of versions that introduce new camera, action, mise-en-scène, shot, or equivalent fresh production.

recomposedVersions.description: Count of adaptations that require material reframing, redesign, or recomposition.
